input.rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or more-favourable-terms obligation burdening us. The only comparative-terms provision is Subparagraph 15.2, which binds the Terminal Parties to furnish transiting facilities to the Parties (including us) on terms no less favorable than those granted to another Carrier — an MFN running in our favour as a capacity holder, not an obligation on us. Teleglobe USA Inc. is not a Terminal Party (it holds no Terminal Station or Cable Landing Point under Paragraphs 10 and 15), so it is a beneficiary rather than the obligor. Related provisions (16.2, 17.1–17.3) likewise impose only reasonable, non-discriminatory access duties on the Terminal Parties. This meets the preferred position (no Customer MFN), so no redline is proposed.
